1	# Secret redaction in run artifacts
 2	
 3	Redact secrets before they reach disk. Apply a configurable redaction pass to tool inputs/outputs and event payloads covering known token shapes (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and the configured authTokenEnv value, sk- prefixed keys, bearer headers, AWS keys, private key blocks, .env assignments) plus user-supplied redact patterns. Replace matches with a stable placeholder that preserves a hash prefix so distinct secrets remain distinguishable in an audit without being recoverable.
 4	
 5	## Rationale
 6	Tool artifacts store full inputs and outputs verbatim, and runs/ is never pruned. Every run that reads a .env or echoes a header writes a live credential to disk permanently — an audit trail that is itself a liability, which blocks sharing run artifacts with the auditors the product targets.
 7	
 8	## User Stories
 9	- [object Object]
10	- [object Object]
11	
12	## Acceptance Criteria
13	- [ ] Redaction is applied in RunStore.append before any write, so events.jsonl, tools/*.txt, gates.json and cost.json are all covered by a single chokepoint
14	- [ ] The resolved auth token value is redacted by exact match regardless of pattern coverage
15	- [ ] Built-in patterns detect sk-* keys, Authorization/Bearer headers, AWS access key ids and secrets, PEM private key blocks, and KEY=value assignments for names matching /TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|KEY/
16	- [ ] config.redact accepts additional user regex patterns, validated at config load with a clear error on an invalid pattern

payload.result:
1	# Vigil
 2	
 3	Agent-SDK TUI runner for gated validation plans and arbitrary prompts. Every tool call, gate verdict, hook decision, token and dollar is visible live in an animated cockpit — and persisted to disk so a run can be replayed or audited without the TUI.
 4	
 5	Built on `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (the Claude Code agent loop) + Ink.
 6	
 7	## Install
 8	
 9	```bash
10	cd ~/Desktop/vigil
11	npm install && npm run build && npm link      # → `vigil` on PATH
12	```
13	
14	Requires Node ≥ 20 and a Claude Code executable (`claude` on PATH, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`, or `--claude-bin`).
15	
16	## Use
17	
18	```bash
19	vigil run ~/Desktop/OmniRoute/_tasks/planning/omp-live-deploy            # every plan, in order, halting on the first FAIL
20	vigil run …/omp-live-deploy --only 01-01                                  # one plan
21	vigil run …/omp-live-deploy --from 02-01 --to 02-02                       # a range
22	vigil prompt "Audit ~/.omniroute/logs for errors in the last hour"        # any prompt, same cockpit
23	vigil prompt -f brief.md --approvals all                                  # approve every tool call by hand
24	vigil replay <planRoot>/runs/<id> --speed 30                              # re-animate a recorded run
25	vigil tail   <planRoot>/runs/<id>                                         # follow a run from another terminal
26	vigil runs   <planRoot>                                                   # list runs with verdict + cost
27	vigil run … --plain                                                       # no TUI: readable line log (CI, ssh, logs)
28	```
29	
30	### Keys
31	
32	`space` pause (holds the next tool call) · `i` inject an instruction into the live session · `x` interrupt the current turn · `a` cycle approvals auto → gates → all · `e` evidence overlay (criteria ‖ captured file) · `t` tool detail (full input/output, `j`/`k` to walk) · `l` diagnostics level · `f` filter by source · `r` re-run a failed plan · `q` quit.
33	
34	## What Vigil enforces (beyond what the agent says)
35	
36	- **Verdict lines.** The runner contract appended to every plan requires `VG-<id>: PASS|FAIL <reason>` and `PLAN <id>: PASS|FAIL`. Vigil parses them from the stream.
37	- **Evidence on disk.** A gate's `Capture:` files must exist and be non-empty in the plan's `evidence/` directory; a claimed PASS with missing evidence is recorded as FAIL and the agent is told to capture for real.
38	- **Rails.** `PreToolUse` hook denies `git stash`, checkout/switch in the shared main checkout, `pkill -f`/`killall`, `rm -rf ~`, edits to `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`; warns on touching the real `~/.omp` config or the live OmniRoute DB. Configurable in `vigil.config.json → rails[]`.
39	- **Reports from observation.** `<phase>-VALIDATION.md` and the ROADMAP status table are written by Vigil from `gates.json`, not from agent prose.
40	
41	## Clean agent by default
42	
43	Vigil runs the agent with `settingSources: []` — none of your Claude Code user/project settings (plugins, hooks, skills, `env` overrides such as coordinator mode or context-size flags) are loaded, so a run is reproducible and its context stays small. Opt back in with `--settings user,project` or `settingSources` in config.
44	
45	## Config (`vigil.config.json` in cwd, or `~/.config/vigil/config.json`)
46	
47	```json
48	{
49	  "model": "cc/claude-fable-5-1",
50	  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1",
51	  "authTokenEnv": "OMNIROUTE_API_KEY",
52	  "cwd": "/Users/nick/Desktop/OmniRoute/.claude/worktrees/omp-cli-tool",
53	  "approvals": "auto",
54	  "maxTurns": 400,
55	  "unsetEnv": ["NODE_ENV"],
56	  "addDirs": ["/Users/nick/.omniroute", "/Users/nick/Library/LaunchAgents", "/Users/nick/.omp"],
57	  "probes": [
58	    { "name": ":20219", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:20219/api/health", "expect": "\"status\":\"ok\"", "intervalSec": 20 },
59	    { "name": ":20128", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:20128/api/health", "intervalSec": 30 },
60	    { "name": "tunnel", "url": "https://router.hack.ski/api/health", "expect": "ok", "intervalSec": 30 },
61	    { "name": "launchd", "command": "launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.omniroute.autostart | grep -q 'state = running'", "intervalSec": 30 }
62	  ]
63	}
64	```
65	
66	## Run artifacts (`<planRoot>/runs/<id>/`)
67	
68	`events.jsonl` (every RunEvent) · `tools/NNNN-<tool>.txt` (full input/output per call) · `gates.json` · `cost.json` (per model) · `session.json` (SDK session ids → `--resume`).
69	
70	## Develop
71	
72	`npm test` (vitest: parser, verdicts, rails, reducer, reports, session enforcement) · `npm run typecheck` · `npm run build`.

1	# Secret redaction in run artifacts
 2	
 3	Redact secrets before they reach disk. Apply a configurable redaction pass to tool inputs/outputs and event payloads covering known token shapes (ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN and the configured authTokenEnv value, sk- prefixed keys, bearer headers, AWS keys, private key blocks, .env assignments) plus user-supplied redact patterns. Replace matches with a stable placeholder that preserves a hash prefix so distinct secrets remain distinguishable in an audit without being recoverable.
 4	
 5	## Rationale
 6	Tool artifacts store full inputs and outputs verbatim, and runs/ is never pruned. Every run that reads a .env or echoes a header writes a live credential to disk permanently — an audit trail that is itself a liability, which blocks sharing run artifacts with the auditors the product targets.
 7	
 8	## User Stories
 9	- [object Object]
10	- [object Object]
11	
12	## Acceptance Criteria
13	- [ ] Redaction is applied in RunStore.append before any write, so events.jsonl, tools/*.txt, gates.json and cost.json are all covered by a single chokepoint
14	- [ ] The resolved auth token value is redacted by exact match regardless of pattern coverage
15	- [ ] Built-in patterns detect sk-* keys, Authorization/Bearer headers, AWS access key ids and secrets, PEM private key blocks, and KEY=value assignments for names matching /TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|KEY/
16	- [ ] config.redact accepts additional user regex patterns, validated at config load with a clear error on an invalid pattern
17	- [ ] Redacted values render as [redacted:<8-char-hash>] so two different secrets remain distinguishable across a run
18	- [ ] Redaction throughput is benchmarked and adds under 10% overhead on a synthetic 10k-event run
19	- [ ] A test writes a fixture tool output containing each supported secret shape and asserts no raw secret survives to disk

Also add an optional `redactEnabled: z.boolean().default(true)` escape hatch for operators who must debug a run with raw artifacts, documented as unsafe. Do not change any other config key. (attempt 1)

# Gotchas and Pitfalls

Things to watch out for in this codebase:

- Ad-hoc tsx scripts must live inside the worktree (relative ./src imports fail from /tmp)
- RegExp 'd' (hasIndices) flag is what makes prefix-preserving capture-group replacement exact; m.indices[i] gives the span
- tests/ is OUTSIDE tsconfig include (["src"]), so `npm run typecheck` does NOT typecheck test files - verify a new test file explicitly with npx tsc --noEmit --strict --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --types node tests/<file>.test.ts
- vitest transpiles tests without typechecking, so a type error in a test file passes `npm test` silently
- Assert a 'literal-only' secret is NOT redacted by the default redactor before asserting a literals-configured redactor redacts it, otherwise the test can pass vacuously
- The redactor preserves readable prefixes (Authorization: Bearer / API_KEY=) and only replaces the capture group, so assertions must not expect the whole line to become a placeholder
- The PEM pattern replaces the entire block including the BEGIN/END markers (no capture group), unlike the assignment patterns
# Code Patterns

Established patterns to follow in this codebase:

- NodeNext module resolution: all intra-src imports must use explicit .js specifiers, types imported with 'import type'
- tsconfig include is ["src"] with rootDir src, so scripts/ and tests/ are outside the build
- Copy-on-change walks (return the same reference when nothing changed) keep hot paths allocation-free
- Tests import source via ../src/... with explicit .js specifiers, same as intra-src imports
- Extract<RunEvent, { kind: 'tool.start' }> is the clean way to type a single event variant in a test factory
- Use a factory function returning a fresh event per test when asserting non-mutation, so tests cannot leak state into each other

Things to watch out for in this codebase:

- zod v4 .default() short-circuits on undefined input, so checks attached before .default() never run for the default value
